proposals.current_tex: We split each dataset into train, validation, and test splits with ratios of 70\%, 15\%, 15\%, respectively. To evaluate the learning capabilities of baselines, we further filter and balance splits such that each split has at least one task that share the same required skill.
proposals.proposed_tex: After iterative rare-skill filtering, 4,987 of 5,400 tasks remain. A constrained global 70\%/15\%/15\% split yields 3,491/748/748 task-disjoint train/validation/test instances, with all 306 retained gold skills represented in each partition; this tests held-out-task rather than unseen-skill generalization (Appendix~\ref{app:data-splits}).
proposals.reason: Replace only the last two sentences of the paragraph. The current per-dataset ratio is inaccurate; the appendix explicitly gives a global constrained allocation and shared skill vocabulary.

evidence.quote: This leaves 4,987 tasks associated with 306 distinct gold skills; 413 tasks are excluded.
We target a global train/validation/test allocation of 70\%/15\%/15\%, yielding 3,491/748/748 tasks.

Task identifiers are disjoint across partitions, but the skill vocabulary is deliberately shared: each partition contains all 306 retained gold skills. The evaluation consequently measures generalization to held-out tasks involving represented skills, rather than to entirely unseen skills.
